title: Retries and a dead-letter path nobody can ignore
description:
**Reworked 2026-11-04:** Ryan reversed the architecture. No new AWS account and no central service; see docs/notifications-plan.md in AnthusAI/Caducus.

**Milestone:** M2, operators finished

**Goal.** As an operator, a message that could not be delivered becomes something I am told about once and can act on. Simpler now: every host's dead-letter queue has a CloudWatch alarm, and in papyrus-production the operator listener already hears it.

**Build.**
- Package: transient errors retry through SQS visibility; permanent errors go straight to `failed` with a reason. `dead_lettered` status, and `caducus notify redrive <queue>`: safe, because the claim row prevents double-sending.
- Hosts: an alarm on age of oldest message per dead-letter queue (PPY-44721a, PPY-e92c8e), with a catalog entry naming the command to run. It clears when the queue is empty. If operator mail itself is what failed, the dead-man covers it.

**Acceptance.**
Force a failure with a poison message in a test; one incident, one clearing after redrive.

**Depends on:** kanbus-d68036, kanbus-1c3618
**Related:** PPY-3e260c

**Specification.**
```gherkin
Feature: Dead letters
  Scenario: A delivery fails repeatedly
    Given a delivery that fails on every attempt
    When retries are exhausted
    Then the log shows "dead_lettered"
    And an operator gets one message naming the queue and the command to redrive

  Scenario: Redrive clears it
    Given a dead-letter incident is open
    When an operator redrives the queue and it empties
    Then one message says it cleared and nothing was sent twice
```
